lead.text: You talk to one main bot. It shares the work between your bots and shows what they did. With the AI you already have, or with free models.
Your bots work together in a team and show what they did. With the AI you already have, or with free models.

what.title: Work you can hand off
what.lead: A few things your bots already do today.

items.title: A summary every morning
items.text: Every weekday at 8:00 a summary, or a report as a PDF in your chat app. If a routine misses its time, you get a notice.

items.title: Answer messages
items.text: Connect Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack or email to a bot. Anything about money or promises goes to you first.

items.title: Search the web
items.text: A bot works in its own browser. You watch live and take over when a login is needed.

items.title: A team per business
items.text: A web shop, a bakery, a project of your own: each with its own bots, files and budget.

items.title: Remember things
items.text: Say “remember that…” and your bots know next time, with the source attached.

items.title: Approve on the go
items.text: Your phone notifies you of a question, you say yes or no. It all runs through your own PC.

memory.title: Your bots remember what you say
memory.text: After a conversation TeamBot keeps facts, preferences and agreements by itself. Every night it tidies up duplicates and expired items.
points: Every item has a source and a date.
Forgetting is real forgetting, and undo is always possible.

points.text: Search by meaning happens on your own PC: ask for a *car* and it also finds *auto*.
Every team has its own memory.

free.title: Limit reached? Keep working for free
free.text: When your Claude or ChatGPT limit runs out, ordinary work continues with a free provider, and last on a model on your own PC. You do not need a subscription to start.
points: Every switch is shown in the chat, and under each answer you see which model gave it.

points.text: A bar at the bottom shows how much is left, with the reset time.
Important work waits rather than carrying on with a weaker model.

free.note: Free models have daily limits, and what is on offer changes often.

Your phone connects to your own PC from anywhere. Your PC has to be on.

points: Your phone gets no keys, and you can disconnect it at any time.

steps.title: Give it a task

principles.title: No silent surprises
principles.lead: With AI bots things often go wrong quietly: a limit that runs out unnoticed, another model without you knowing, or a task marked *done* when nothing happened. TeamBot shows what is going on.

items.title: Your usage always in view
items.text: A bar at the bottom shows how much is left of your Claude and Codex limits and which free sources are available, with the reset time.

items.title: Keep working when a model runs out
items.text: When a limit or a free model runs out, ordinary work continues with another free provider, or else on your own PC.

items.title: Important work would rather wait
items.text: An important task doesn't carry on with a weaker model. It pauses, says why and until when, and then continues by itself.

items.title: You see which model answered
items.text: Every answer shows the model and the cost. When a bot switches, it says so in the chat.

items.title: Done means done, with proof
items.text: Before a task goes to *done*, a second check reviews the work and attaches the proof. Without proof it says *to check*.

items.title: Simple, unless you want more
items.text: A calm screen with a few fixed places. What you don't need every day is under *Advanced*.

compare.switchText: Your bots, routines, skills and memories come over in one go. OpenBot is left untouched.

price.title: TeamBot costs nothing
price.text: No account, no subscription and no credits. You only pay for what you choose yourself, directly to that party: your own AI subscription or the use of an API key. With free or local models you pay nothing.

items.title: On your own PC
items.text: Conversations, memory and files are on your computer. You don't need an account with us, and TeamBot sends us nothing.

items.title: Only to the AI you choose
items.text: A bot only sends what it needs for its answer, to the AI service you picked for that bot. With a local model nothing goes to an AI service.

items.title: You decide
items.text: Sending, paying and deleting ask first. Keys are encrypted, and one button stops everything.

honest.title: Honestly: what it can't do yet

items.text: The installer isn't signed yet. That's why Windows warns you the first time.

items: Your bots work as long as your PC is on and TeamBot is running.

items.text: Windows only. There is no app in the App Store or Play Store; your phone uses TeamBot through the browser.
Windows only. The iPhone app is still in testing and not in the App Store; otherwise you use TeamBot on your phone through the browser.

items: Free models have daily limits, and what is on offer changes often.

cta.title: Try it on your own PC
cta.text: Free and open source, no account.

items.teaser: One front door that spreads the work over separate teams.
items.title: One main bot, separate teams

what.text: You talk to one main bot. It passes the work to the right team and reports back, with proof. Each team, for example per business or project, has its own folder, memory, budget and log.
Create a team per business or project. Each team has its own folder, memory, budget and log, with a team lead and a shared task board.

why: You don't have to remember which bot does what: you just ask your main bot.
A bot only sees another team if you allow it: *no access*, *watch* or *direct*.
With one team you see nothing of teams. The team picker only appears with your second team.
items.start: Choose *Main bot* for your first bot. You create a second team with *New team* in the team picker. More in [Teams](page:manual#teams) (in Dutch).

items.teaser: Bots that keep learning in their field, with source and date.
items.title: Specialists that keep learning
items.what: Turn a bot into a specialist in a field, such as purchasing, SEO or taxes. In a learning round it fetches new content from sources you choose, and keeps the essence in its own knowledge base.
why: Every fact has a source and a date, and everything can be undone.
If something new contradicts what it already knows, it goes to *To check*.
Your corrections become lessons for the whole team, and a way of working that often goes well becomes a skill proposal.
items.start: In the bot settings, under *Advanced › Specialism*, switch on the option *Specialist in a field* and fill in the field and the sources. The learning round stays off until you switch it on. More in [Specialists](page:manual#specialisten) (in Dutch).

items.teaser: Remembers what you say, with a source, and keeps itself up to date.
items.title: A memory that keeps itself up to date
items.what: After a conversation TeamBot remembers facts, preferences and agreements from what you said. Every night it clears out duplicates and expired items, and facts that change over time are checked again.
why: Every item has a source. Under an answer you see where a memory came from.
Forgetting really forgets, and undo always works.

why.text: Search by meaning happens on your own PC: ask about a *vehicle* and it also finds *car*.
Every team has its own memory. A bot takes nothing along to another team.

items.start: Say “remember that …” in a conversation, or look under *Memory* at what is already there. More in [Memory and case files](page:manual#geheugen-en-dossiers) (in Dutch).

items.teaser: When a limit runs out, TeamBot carries on for free. A bar shows it all.
items.title: Keep working for free, and always see what is left
items.what: When your Claude or ChatGPT limit runs out, ordinary work carries on with a free provider, and as a last step on a model on your own PC. The usage bar at the bottom always shows how much is left.
why: Every switch is mentioned in the chat, and every answer shows which model gave it.

why.text: Above a threshold you choose (85% of your week by default), ordinary work moves to free models early, so enough is left for important work.
The bar is green, orange or red, with the reset time. When a provider gives no exact figure, it says *estimate*.

items.start: The chain is on by default. Switch on free sources under *Settings › Free models*. More in [Free models](page:manual#gratis-modellen) and [The usage bar](page:manual#de-gebruiksbalk) (in Dutch).

items.teaser: Your main bot in your pocket, with a notification when it has a question.
items.title: Your bots on your phone

what.text: Add TeamBot as an app to the home screen of your iPhone or Android. You talk to your main bot, approve what is waiting for you and get a notification when there is a question. Your phone only talks to your own PC.

With the iPhone app (still in testing) or as an app on the home screen of any phone. You talk to your main bot, approve what is waiting for you and get a notification when there is a question. Your phone only talks to your own PC.

why: Almost everything you can do on your PC works on your phone too: chat, approve, bots, routines and teams.
Your phone gets no keys, and you can always unpair it.

why.text: It connects at home over your own wifi, or anywhere through Tailscale (free for personal use). Your PC needs to be on.
Your phone connects to your own PC from anywhere. Your PC needs to be on.

start.text: Install Tailscale on your PC and your phone, go to *Settings › Phone* and scan the QR code. More in [Your phone](page:manual#je-telefoon) (in Dutch).
Go to *Settings › Phone* and scan the QR code. More in [Your phone](page:manual#je-telefoon) (in Dutch).

items.teaser: Talk to your bots from Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack and more.
items.title: Talk to your bots in the chat app you already use
items.what: Connect Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, Slack or e-mail to a bot or to your main bot. You send a message and your bot replies in the same app, with a PDF attached if needed.
why: Only senders you allow get in. Others get no tools.
A channel is only called *connected* once TeamBot has really received and sent a message.

why.text: Bots that talk to customers say they are AI. Anything about money, prices or promises goes to you first.

items.start: *Settings › Channels › Add channel*. Telegram is the easiest: your own bot, without an open port. More in [Channels](page:manual#kanalen-whatsapp-telegram-en-meer) (in Dutch).

items.teaser: Ready-made ways of working, on pinned versions and with a licence.
items.title: Skills: ways of working for your bots
items.what: A skill is a way of working a bot follows, such as sorting a customer question or making a campaign plan. A bot only loads a skill when a task asks for it.

why.text: Skills come from TeamBot's own catalogue on pinned versions, with maker and licence in view.

why: You read a skill before you install it, with a safety check. You see an update as a diff first.
Did something work well in a conversation? With *Save as skill* you make one yourself, for one bot or the whole team.
Apps (MCP) first get read access only; then you choose per bot what it may do.
items.start: Open *Marketplace › Skills*, pick a skill and switch it on for a bot or team. More in [Skills and apps](page:manual#skills-en-apps) (in Dutch).

items.teaser: Regular tasks at fixed times, with proof that they ran.
items.title: Routines that tell you what happened
items.what: Let a bot do something at fixed times, such as an overview every working day at 8:00, or the invoices on the last working day of the month. Or let a routine start on a new file, an e-mail, a webhook or a chat message.

why.text: A run only counts as successful with a result. If it didn't run, you get a notification: “expected at 08:00, did not run”.

why: The calendar shows per week or month what is planned and what happened.
The result can go to your chat app, for example your daily report as a PDF.
items.start: Say “remind me every Monday at 9 about …” in the chat, or choose *Routines › New routine*. More in [Routines](page:manual#routines) (in Dutch).

items.teaser: Its own browser for every bot. Your desktop only if you want.
items.title: Its own browser, and your desktop only if you want
items.what: A bot works on the web in its own browser, with its own profile. You watch live and take over to sign in yourself. Letting it use your own desktop is off by default.
why: Sign-in windows, password managers and banking and payment windows always stay closed.
If you switch the desktop on, you choose which apps, and the bot asks at every action by default.
Move the mouse and the bot pauses. Emergency stop: `Ctrl+Alt+Esc`.
items.start: Per bot, under *Advanced › Computer & files*, choose the least it needs, for example *Own browser*. More in [Browser and computer use](page:manual#browser-en-computer-use) (in Dutch).

items.teaser: Everything stays on your own PC. No account, no telemetry.
items.title: Everything on your own PC
items.what: Your bots, conversations, memory and files are on your own computer. You don't need an account with us, and TeamBot sends the makers nothing: no statistics and no crash reports.
why: A bot only sends what it needs for its answer, to the AI you picked for that bot.

why.text: Every source has a label: *stays on your PC*, *keeps nothing* or *may train*.

why: Keys are encrypted and never appear in conversations, logs or exports.
Sending, paying and deleting ask for your permission first.
items.start: Click the padlock at the bottom of the sidebar: *Where is my data?* shows per bot what leaves your PC. Everything in one place is on [Safety and privacy](page:privacy).

items.teaser: Light or dark, and a colour of your choice on all your devices.
items.title: Your colour, light or dark
items.what: Choose light, dark or system, and one of ten colours or *Standard*. You immediately see a light and a dark preview side by side.
why: The colour applies on your PC, in the browser and on your phone.
Every colour meets the WCAG AA contrast standard, so text stays easy to read.
Your bots keep their own figure and colour, smooth or felt.
items.start: *Settings › Appearance › Colour*. More in [Language and other settings](page:manual#taal-en-overige-instellingen) (in Dutch).

more.title: And also
more.lead: Smaller, but you notice it every day.

items.title: Done with proof
items.text: Every task says when it is done. A second check reviews the work; without proof it says *to check*.

items.title: Voice, local and free
items.text: Dictation, also in other programs, reading aloud and talking with your bots. On your own PC.

items.title: You choose what a bot may do
items.text: Five levels, from chat only to full access. Sending and paying always ask first.

items.title: Recycle bin and rehearsal
items.text: If a bot deletes a file, you get it back. Or let it work on a copy of a folder first.

items.title: Eleven languages
items.text: The app works in eleven languages, including Arabic. Your bots answer in the language you write in.

items.title: Backups with a way back
items.text: A backup every day, and before every update. Restoring takes one click.

limits.title: What it can't do yet
limits.lead: These are the known limitations of version {version}:

items.text: The Windows installer isn't signed yet; that's why Windows warns you the first time.

items: TeamBot is Windows only. There is no tested package for macOS or Linux.
Your bots run on your own PC or server. When it is off, they stop.

items.text: Your phone connects at home over wifi or anywhere through Tailscale; from anywhere without Tailscale isn't possible yet.
There is no app in the App Store or Play Store. Your phone uses TeamBot through the browser.
The iPhone app is for testers only (TestFlight) and not in the App Store. There is no Android app; Android uses the browser.

items: Free models have limits per day or per hour, and what is on offer changes often. Small local models make more mistakes than large ones.
Claude and Codex limits are partly estimated, and they are shared with your own use of Claude and ChatGPT outside TeamBot.
A bot that uses your desktop shares the mouse and keyboard with you.
WhatsApp through a QR code is an unofficial connection. WhatsApp may block such a number; for a business the official WhatsApp Business connection is the safe choice.
Some connections are built and tested automatically, but not yet with a real account or device. Which ones is listed in the [manual](page:manual#wat-nog-niet-kan) (in Dutch).
Accessibility has been tested with axe-core and the keyboard, not yet with a screen reader.

ours.title: Truly open source
ours.text: Apache-2.0: use, change and share it, also for business. OpenBot is non-commercial; Grok Bot, ChatGPT, Claude, Manus and Lindy are closed.

ours.title: Keep working for free
ours.text: The free chain is on by default, and important work pauses instead of quietly switching to a weaker model.

ours.title: Done means done
ours.text: Every task has a *done when* and a second check with proof.

ours.title: Safe by default

ours.title: On your own PC

ours.title: Routines that don't fail silently

comes.title: Your team over in one go

items.title: Bots
items.text: Name, instructions, model and reasoning level, backups in order, access and face.

items.title: Routines
items.text: Every schedule. They arrive switched **off**, so nothing runs twice.

items.title: Your own skills

items.title: Memories

items.title: Team tables and team folder
items.text: Tasks, decisions and log. Your shared folder becomes the team folder, without a copy.

text.text: Your boss becomes the main bot or team lead; a knowledge bot becomes a specialist.
Your boss becomes team lead; a knowledge bot becomes a specialist.

not.title: What doesn't come along

items.title: Conversations and attachments
items.text: A deliberate choice: you start clean. They stay in OpenBot.

items.title: Keys, tokens and passwords
items.text: Never. You sign in again or paste your key again.

items.title: Channels and apps
items.text: You connect them again in TeamBot. Read [Telegram and WhatsApp](page:switch#channels) first.

items.title: OpenBot's own skills

steps.title: In six steps
steps.lead: Allow about a quarter of an hour. OpenBot can keep running in the meantime.

items.title: Install TeamBot
items.text: [Download](page:download) and install TeamBot on the same PC as OpenBot.

items.title: See what comes over
items.text: The welcome screen shows *Move your OpenBot team* (later under *Settings › Switching*). Click *See what comes over* and *Read OpenBot*: TeamBot only reads.

items.title: Choose what comes along
items.text: Tick what should come along. Choose the team, who becomes main bot or team lead and which bots become specialists, and a work folder per bot: the existing folder (recommended), a copy or a new empty folder.

items.title: Import
items.text: Click *Import*. Then you see an overview, with *Undo import* if you want to go back after all.

items.title: Connect your AI and your phone
items.text: TeamBot finds Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode on this PC by itself. Paste an API key again under *Settings › AI services*. Pair your phone with a QR code.

items.title: Switch on your channels and routines
items.text: Stopping with OpenBot? Move your chat apps over as described below, and click *Switch on routines*.

channels.title: One channel, one app at a time
channels.lead: A Telegram bot or WhatsApp number can only be connected to one app at a time. Telegram refuses the second app, and with WhatsApp both apps could answer the same message.
steps: Disconnect the channel in OpenBot, or close OpenBot.
In TeamBot choose *Settings › Channels › Add channel* and pick the same channel.
Telegram: paste your bot token. WhatsApp through QR: scan the code on your phone under *Linked devices*.
Send a test message. The channel is only called *connected* once TeamBot has really received and sent a message.
channels.tip: **Want to try it first?** Create a second Telegram bot for TeamBot with @BotFather. Then OpenBot keeps working on your old bot.

cards.title: Telegram
text: A bot token can only be read by one app at a time. If two apps use it, TeamBot reports a conflict: another app is already using this bot token.
Lost your token? Ask @BotFather for a new one; the old one stops working.

cards.title: WhatsApp
text: In WhatsApp on your phone, under *Linked devices*, remove OpenBot's link, then scan TeamBot's QR code.
WhatsApp through QR is unofficial and WhatsApp may block such a number. For a business, *WhatsApp Business (Cloud API)* is the safe choice.

items.title: You can always go back
items.text: *Undo import* removes what the import created. OpenBot itself was never changed.

items.title: Read again
items.text: Want something more later? Read OpenBot again; what is already there won't be doubled.

items.title: Access as you had it
items.text: If a bot had full access in OpenBot, it gets that in TeamBot too. Sending and paying still ask first.

end.title: Ready to switch?
end.text: Free, open source and no account. OpenBot stays until you decide.

items.q: Is TeamBot free?
a: Yes. TeamBot costs €0: no account, no subscription, no trial period and no credits. The code is open source under the Apache-2.0 licence.
You only pay for what you choose yourself, directly to that party: your own AI subscription or the use of an API key. With free or local models you pay nothing. See [Pricing](page:pricing).

items.q: Which AI do I need?
a: None, to begin with: *Start for free* sets up a free model, without an account.

Do you have Claude Pro or Max, or ChatGPT Plus or Pro? Then TeamBot uses the official Claude Code or Codex on your own login. You can also paste an API key, or with a fast PC run a model on your own computer (Ollama or LM Studio).

items.q: What do I need to install it?
items.a: A PC with Windows 11 (64-bit), or Windows 10 with ESU or LTSC support. Mac and Linux aren't supported yet; your own server with Docker is. See [Download](page:download#req).

items.q: Why does Windows warn me when installing?
items.a: The installer isn't signed yet. Only download it from the official release page, click **More info** in the blue window and then **Run anyway**.

items.q: Do I need to know how to program?
items.a: No. Creating a bot asks three things: a name, what it does and which model. The rest has good defaults.

items.q: Is my data safe?
a: Your bots, conversations, memory and files are on your own PC, in `%APPDATA%\TeamBot`. You don't need an account with us and TeamBot sends the makers nothing: no statistics, no crash reports.

A bot only sends what it needs for its answer to the AI service you picked for that bot. With a local model nothing goes to an AI service. Keys are encrypted. Read [exactly how it works](page:privacy).

items.q: Can bots just do things?
items.a: A new bot asks permission first. Sending to others and paying always ask, even with *full access*. One button stops all bots.

items.q: Do AI services use my data for training?

a.text: That depends on the service. In TeamBot every source has a label: *stays on your PC*, *keeps nothing* or *may train*. Some free services may use what you send to improve their models; keep sensitive work on a local model.
That depends on the service. Some free services may use what you send to improve their models; keep sensitive work on a local model.

items.q: How do I remove everything?
items.a: Export what you want to keep, unpair your phone and chat apps, and remove TeamBot through Windows. Then choose **Yes** to delete your data too. The steps are on [Safety and privacy](page:privacy#delete).

items.q: Does it work on my phone without Tailscale?

a.text: At home it does: on the same wifi network as your PC. That connection isn't encrypted and gives no push notifications.

Away from home you need Tailscale for now. It is free for personal use and gives an encrypted connection between your own devices. Connecting from anywhere without Tailscale isn't in this version yet.
Yes. Your phone connects to your own PC from anywhere, also without Tailscale. Your PC does need to be on.

items.q: Is there an app in the App Store or Play Store?

a.text: No. You add TeamBot to your home screen from the browser: on iPhone with Safari › Share › *Add to Home Screen*, on Android with Chrome › *Install app*. Then it works like an app, with notifications.
Not in the stores yet. The iPhone app is in testing through TestFlight; otherwise you add TeamBot to your home screen from the browser, with notifications.

items.q: Does my PC have to stay on?
items.a: Yes. Your bots run on your own PC or server. When it is off they stop, and TeamBot reports routines that didn't run because of it. Switch on *Keep the PC awake while routines or tasks run* if you like.

items.q: What happens when my limit runs out?

a.text: You see it coming in the usage bar. Ordinary work continues on a free or local model, and every answer shows which model gave it. Work with the *Important* switch waits until your limit is back.
You choose per bot: switch to a backup, wait until the limit is back, or stop. Every answer shows which model gave it.

items.q: Can I use OpenBot and TeamBot side by side?
items.a: Yes. The import only reads OpenBot, and routines arrive switched off. A Telegram bot or WhatsApp number is connected to one app at a time, though. See [Switching from OpenBot](page:switch).

items.q: Which languages does TeamBot work in?
items.a: The app works in 11 languages, including English, Dutch, German, French and Arabic. Your bots answer in the language you write in. The manual is in Dutch.

items.q: May I use TeamBot for business?
items.a: Yes, the Apache-2.0 licence allows that, including changing and sharing it. Do check your AI service's own terms.

end.title: Another question?
end.text: The manual explains every screen, in short steps (in Dutch).

you.title: What you might pay yourself
you.lead: TeamBot needs an AI to work with. You choose it yourself, and you pay that party directly. TeamBot earns nothing from it.

options.title: Free models
options.text: OpenCode with a free model, and free tiers of providers with your own free key. They have limits per day or per hour, and what is on offer changes often.

options.title: Locally on your PC
options.text: With Ollama or LM Studio the model runs on your own computer. You only pay for the electricity. This needs a fast PC, and small models make more mistakes.

options.title: Your own AI subscription
options.text: Claude through Claude Code or ChatGPT through Codex, on your own login. You pay your subscription to Anthropic or OpenAI, as you already did. Your plan's limits apply, including to what you do outside TeamBot.

options.title: An API key
options.text: For example at OpenAI, Anthropic or OpenRouter. You pay that provider per use. TeamBot checks your daily budget before every step; the last step can still go slightly over.

extras: **Your phone away from home** goes through Tailscale. For personal use that is free.
**Your own server** for TeamBot with friends or a team: whatever your hosting company charges.
**A cloud VM** for a bot (Hetzner or DigitalOcean): TeamBot shows the cost before you create it.

items.title: Always see what is left
items.text: The usage bar shows your Claude and Codex limits and the free sources, with the reset time. You get a notification at 80% and at the limit.

items.title: A reserve for important work
items.text: Above a threshold you choose, 85% of your Claude week by default, ordinary work moves to free models early.

items.title: Pausing instead of switching quietly
items.text: An important task doesn't quietly carry on with a weaker model. It waits, and says until when.

items.title: Model and cost under every answer
items.text: With every answer you see which model gave it and what it cost, or *unknown*.

items.title: A daily budget
items.text: Set an amount per day for paid keys. A bot tells you when it is used up.

items.q: Is TeamBot really free?
items.a: Yes. There is no paid version, no trial period and no account. The code is under the Apache-2.0 licence.

items.q: Will there be a paid version later?
items.a: Under the Apache-2.0 licence you may always use every released version for free. If a paid extra service is ever added, such as hosting, its price will be on this page, up front and in plain words.

items.q: Do I pay TeamBot for Claude or ChatGPT?
items.a: No. TeamBot drives the official Claude Code and Codex on your own login. You pay your subscription to Anthropic or OpenAI.

items.q: What happens when my limit runs out?
items.a: You see it coming in the usage bar. Ordinary work continues on a free or local model, and every answer shows which model gave it. Important work waits until your limit is back.

items.q: What happens when my limit runs out?
items.a: You choose per bot: switch to a backup, wait until the limit is back, or stop. Every answer shows which model gave it.

items.q: Are free models really free?
items.a: Yes, but with limits: a number of requests per day or per hour, and an offer that changes often. Some free services may use what you send to improve their models. Keep sensitive work on your own PC with a local model.

items.q: May I use TeamBot for business?
items.a: Yes, the Apache-2.0 licence allows that. Do check your AI service's own terms.

summary.title: On your own PC
summary.text: Your bots, conversations, memory and files are stored on your own computer.

summary.title: To the AI you choose
summary.text: Only what a bot needs for its answer, and only to that bot's service.

summary.title: Keys encrypted
summary.text: Never in conversations, logs or exports, and never on your phone.

summary.title: Everything can be deleted
summary.text: Export what you want to keep and remove the rest in a few steps.

pc.title: What stays on your PC
items: Your bots, conversations, memory, routines, backups and files are in TeamBot's data folder: `%APPDATA%\TeamBot`. Your bots' work folders are there too, unless you picked another folder yourself.
You don't need an account with the makers of TeamBot.
TeamBot sends the makers nothing: no statistics, no crash reports. You create the diagnostics file yourself and only share it if you want to; it contains no messages or keys.
With a local model (Ollama or LM Studio) your conversations don't go to an AI service, and local voice stays on your PC too.

items.text: Every team has its own folder, memory and log. A bot only sees another team if you give it access.

ai.title: What goes to which AI provider
ai.lead: A bot only sends what it needs for its answer: your message, its instructions, and what it uses for that, such as a few memories, parts of files it reads and the output of its tools. That goes to the service you picked for that bot.
ai.caption: Where your message goes, per choice
rows: None: your message doesn't leave your computer
The provider of the model you pick, through OpenCode
Those of OpenCode and that provider
That provider, for example OpenAI, Anthropic or OpenRouter
Their terms; some free services may use what you send to improve their models
after: Never sent: your keys and passwords.

after.text: Also never sent: anything from a team that bot has no access to.
In TeamBot every source has a label: *stays on your PC*, *keeps nothing* or *may train*. The label follows the provider's terms; if in doubt, read them yourself.
Work you mark as private, such as personal data or a sensitive case file, only goes to a local model or to a source that keeps nothing.

after: Every answer shows which model gave it. When a bot switches to another model, it says so.

other.title: What else leaves your PC, only when you use it
items: **Web search:** through DuckDuckGo by default, or a search service you pick yourself.
**Skills and apps:** the catalogue and the files of a skill or app come from where the maker publishes them, such as GitHub.
**Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode:** if you install or update them from TeamBot, it downloads them from the npm registry and checks them first.
**Chat apps:** messages via Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, Slack or e-mail go through those services themselves.
**Your phone:** only talks to your own PC, over your own network or through Tailscale (an encrypted connection between your own devices). What you say goes to your PC, not to the internet.
**Voice:** stays on your PC, unless you pick a live voice or a provider's voice.
**Updates:** TeamBot checks whether there is a new version and only downloads after your click.

keys.title: Keys and sign-ins
items: API keys and other secrets are encrypted in one vault. On Windows, the key for that belongs to your Windows account.
Keys never appear in conversations, logs, exports or the diagnostics file.

items.text: A key works in all your teams by default. You can also limit it to one team.

items: You sign in to Claude Code and Codex yourself. Those programs keep their own sign-in, as always; TeamBot drives them unchanged and sends your sign-in nowhere.
Your phone gets no keys. A paired phone only has its own access pass, which you can always revoke in TeamBot.
If you restore a backup on another PC, you enter your keys again.

control.title: What bots may do
items: For each bot you choose an access level: chat only, read-only, ask first, automatic or full access.
Actions with consequences, such as sending to others, paying and deleting, ask first, and you see what the bot wants to do. That is built into the app, not just into the bot's instructions.
TeamBot treats web pages, e-mails and messages from other bots as information, not as instructions.
Letting a bot use your desktop is off by default. Sign-in screens, password managers and payment windows always stay closed.
Images and link previews from bots only load after a click, so a bot can't send data away through a web address.
Everything with consequences is in the log, and one button stops all bots.
control.note: A work folder is not a sealed environment: TeamBot only claims isolation where it really exists. The full threat model is in [docs/THREAT_MODEL.md](repo:docs/THREAT_MODEL.md).

delete.title: Deleting everything
delete.lead: This is how you remove TeamBot and your data completely:
steps: Want to keep something? In TeamBot, choose *Settings › Data › Export*.
Unpair your phone and your chat apps in TeamBot. After that the link works nowhere, even if the app is still on your phone.
Remove TeamBot through Windows *Settings › Apps*. The installer asks whether you also want to delete your data; choose **Yes**. The default is *No*, so a reinstall loses nothing.
Did you choose *No* earlier, or give a bot a work folder outside the data folder? Then delete those folders yourself, such as `%APPDATA%\TeamBot`.

What was already sent to an AI service or chat app falls under that service. Delete it there, for example in your account at Anthropic or OpenAI, and sign out of Claude Code and Codex if you no longer use them.

site.title: This website
items: No cookies, no trackers, no analytics and no fonts or scripts from other servers.
Your choice of light or dark is only stored in your own browser.
The party hosting this site may keep technical server logs, such as IP address and time. Which party that is will be stated here once the site is online.
